proof_attempt_summary: The run repaired a false equality-versus-dominance collision, obtained field-level proposal acceptance, and derived sound preliminary finite-error brackets with verified citations. The original-record and supplied-allocation logarithmic gaps and the order of J_n remain unresolved, so the completed package is incremental and below the field floor. No Lean formalization was attempted; retry requires new presolved test, covariance/bias, and matching lower-family evidence rather than replaying the same multiscale suggestion.
tldr: Conditional stochastic dominance requires the treated law to dominate the baseline at every covariate and threshold. The internal \texttt{stat\_quarterholder\_allocation\_testing} frontier tests conditional equality with two-sided integrated absolute CDF separation; this proposal tests the full cone \(F_{P,1}\le F_{P,0}\) with one-sided integrated positive-part separation \(\rho\). Equality calibration can reject legal strict-dominance laws, and equality lower alternatives need not be one-sided-separated. The central question therefore requires uniform one-sided full-cone size calibration and a cone-valid normalized converse in both original-record and same-record supplied-allocation experiments, with evaluated sharp radii and their information comparison. Arbitrary overlapping allocation, compact laws and atoms remain; half-H\"older Wasserstein regularity is secondary rather than the source of novelty. The presolve brackets are supporting claims to prove.
gap: The persisted internal equality frontier uses \(\Delta\) and the equality null; it does not deliver full-cone size control or a normalized \(\rho\)-separated converse. Published conditional-dominance tests and cone-inference frameworks do not, in the carried source receipts, evaluate both requested finite-error marked-experiment radii on the maintained compact-law class. This bounded literature inference is not an exhaustive priority certificate.
fill: The research output is uniform one-sided full-cone size calibration with an evaluated sharp attainer and cone-valid normalized converses in both marked experiments. It must close both logarithmic gaps and determine the allocation-information ratio without adding regularity. No novelty is attributed to changing a H\"older exponent or restricting an equality model to a smoother subclass.
